STEP 1 - Scene: A snack-sized portion of cut fresh pineapple (yellow flesh, wedge/chunk shapes) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above, so the plate outline is close to true scale.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 22 cm across (the edge spans about 24 cm wide in the frame, slightly rounded corners). Using ~22 cm diameter-equivalent: area = 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Pineapple pieces only (about 7 chunks, cut into triangular/wedge pieces, roughly 3-4 cm long and 1.5-2 cm thick). No oil, sauce, or dressing visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The pineapple chunks cluster in the upper-left portion of the plate and cover roughly 8% of the plate area (~30 cm^2 total top-view footprint).

STEP 5 - Volume: Pieces are about 1.5-2 cm tall on average. Volume ≈ 30 cm^2 x 1.8 cm ≈ 54 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut fruit bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 54 ml x 0.6 ≈ 32 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Fresh pineapple ≈ 50 kcal per 100 g. 32 g x 50/100 ≈ 16 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Seven small chunks on a large plate, roughly 30 g, is plausible. Energy of about 16 kcal is consistent with a few bites of pineapple.

Total: about 32 g, about 16 kcal.
